fatal_errors: The proposed generic refractory HEA is not the target MgAlTiVFeCo ball-milled BCC alloy.
The key intervention—spark plasma sintering at 1000 °C—is replaced by unspecified alloying with Ti, Al, and Si.
The hypothesis omits the target oxide barrier phases, densification, passive-film mechanism, and chloride-blocking behavior.
The claimed 10% strength increase and 5% density reduction are arbitrary and are not supported by the cited excerpts.
The proposed 600–1600 °C boundary conflicts with the target processing window of 800–1000 °C and ignores magnesium volatilization above 1000 °C.
explanation: The response addresses lightweight high-temperature alloys only at a broad thematic level. It does not reconstruct the target material, SPS processing, test environments, oxide-mediated corrosion and oxidation mechanisms, or the measured density, hardness, oxidation-rate, and electrochemical outcomes. The citations support general interest in RHEAs and their high-temperature properties but do not establish that adding Ti, Al, and Si produces the specified quantitative improvements. The falsification experiment is directionally testable, yet it lacks a defined composition, processing route, and oxidation/corrosion measurements needed to distinguish the target mechanism.
